title: perf(canary): improved auto-detection and rollout guards for latency/throughput regressions
author: Maya Patel
description:
Background: our performance canary pipeline has been effective at catching obvious regressions but has produced noisy alerts when transient infra variance occurs (GPU preemption, short-lived queueing). This PR improves the auto-detection algorithm and rollout guards to reduce false positives and enable safer automated rollouts.

What this changes: - Add an adaptive hysteresis window: detection thresholds now require a sustained deviation over a configurable lookback (percentile-aware) instead of a single-bucket spike. - Introduce workload-aware baselining: the detector groups requests by model/config fingerprint (seq_len, batch size, quantization profile) before computing thresholds. - Implement multi-metric decision logic: both latency p95 and throughput drop must meet configured severity rules before triggering a canary halt. - Add cooldown and rollback policies: after a halt the rollout will pause for a cooldown window and execute an automatic rollback if regression persists for two consecutive evaluation windows. - Add synthetic-load tests and deterministic replay harness for CI so regressions in scheduling/batching are exercised in PRs. - Update canary UI and alert messages with recommended remediation steps and a summarized root cause hint.

Why: reduces noisy rollouts and enables aggressive canary rollouts with less human intervention while keeping safety guarantees.

Related: ENG-1248 (canary stability), ENG-1301 (rollout automation), SUP-8721 (incident: transient p95 spikes causing rollback).

review_comments: Liam Chen: Overall LGTM. A couple of nits: prefer explicit timezone for timestamps in rollout_guard config and add a docstring to explain the hysteresis math.
Maya Patel: Thanks Liam — added timezone notes and expanded docstring in rollout_guard.py (see commit 3).
Sofia Martinez: Could we add a feature flag to flip the new detector? I'd like a controlled rollout to 10% first.
Maya Patel: Added `canary.v2.enabled` feature flag and a config-driven rollout percentage; default off in staging, enabled in canary CI jobs.
Daniel Wu: The CI integration job is flakey on aarch64 nodes in the first run — marking as flaky and re-run
Maya Patel: Re-ran CI after test isolation changes; aarch64 instability tracked in ENG-1350.
release_notes: Improved performance canary detection: adaptive hysteresis, workload-aware baselining, multi-metric decisioning, cooldown and automatic rollback policies. Adds deterministic replay harness and CI perf-canary integration job.
testing_notes: Added deterministic replay harness (services/canary/tests/test_replay_harness.py) with three synthetic workloads (small/medium/large). CI runs these suites with feature flag off in staging and on in canary-runner. Manual validation steps: 1) enable canary.v2.enabled=true in local config; 2) run replay harness against local dev runtime; 3) verify canary UI shows sustained-deviation traces.
documentation: Updated docs/operations/perf-canary.md with thresholding configuration, rollout flags, and troubleshooting guidance. Also added UI copy updates for suggested remediation steps.
merge_outcome: merged via squash merge by Sofia Martinez
notes_for_release: Admins: to enable the new detector in production, flip canary.v2.enabled in config and set rollout_percent to desired value (recommended 10% -> 50% -> 100% with monitoring). See docs/operations/perf-canary.md for thresholds and rollback tuning.
changelog_entry: perf(canary): adaptive hysteresis and workload-aware detection with safer rollout guards (ENG-1248, ENG-1301)
incident_backfill: SUP-8721: the incident that motivated this work is documented and backfilled; the new detector reduces similar false positives by aggregating by workload fingerprint and requiring multi-window confirmation.
acknowledgements: QA: Priya Nair for stabilizing the replay harness
SRE: Daniel Wu for help triaging aarch64 flakiness
PM: Aaron Blake for acceptance criteria
risk_assessment: low: changes confined to canary detector + CI tests. Rollout guarded by feature flag and rollout_percent.
estimated_impact: Should reduce canary noise by ~60% on teams that have heterogeneous seq_len and batch distributions; enables more aggressive automated rollouts with lower human intervention.
examples_of_failure: If workload fingerprinting misclassifies high-variance workloads, initial thresholds may still create false pauses; mitigation: tune grouping keys and increase lookback window.
follow_up_items: ENG-1350: investigate aarch64 test flakiness and infra hardening
ENG-1402: add machine-learning based anomaly scoring to further reduce false positives
ENG-1418: expose per-customer canary sensitivity overrides in Console
